patch_description: Builds on the Gen-31 style bidirectional constant-velocity Kalman fusion (high accuracy, correlation 0.93) and improves noise reduction — the weakest unsaturated metric — by replacing the instantaneous innovation-based R with an EWMA-smoothed measurement-noise variance: `R[k] = 0.5·σ_r² + 0.5·ewma_var`, `ewma_var = 0.9·ewma_var + 0.1·innov[k]²`. This widens R during noisy bursts (heavier smoothing exactly where noise dominates) and tightens it during clean segments (preserving dynamics and low lag), without adding any pipeline stage. The state update keeps the pure Kalman form `x_est = xp[k] + K·innov` with the symmetrized covariance update — no trend-lean or signal-shaping terms, which prior generations showed poison the output. Post-processing retains the zero-lag bidirectional one-pole smoothers plus the noise-scaled slope deadzone, which directly reduce slope changes and false reversals. Key parameters: EWMA forgetting factor 0.9, 50/50 blend between static σ_r² and adaptive ewma_var, Q = (0.02, 0.005), deadzone threshold 0.5·σ_r with 20% leak-through, bidirectional one-pole alphas (0.35–0.70 SNR-adaptive, then +0.15, then 0.75). This targets pushing noise_reduction from 0.54 toward saturation while keeping lag_error low and slope changes low.
